start.speaker: Kronos
start.text: Welcome my friend, I hope your paws are steady. Hanafuda is an ancient Japanese card game, tradition, elegance, and gambling all mixed together.

HTD2.speaker: Kronos
HTD2.text: Perfect for a refined creature like me… and for you, I guess.

HTD3.speaker: Kronos
HTD3.text: Don't worry, if you lose, you only lose your soul. I'm joking! …mostly.

HTD4.speaker: Kronos
HTD4.text: Before we begin, see these eight cards?

HTD5.speaker: Kronos
HTD5.text: Pick one, choose wisely... or don't. It's random anyway. Whoever flips the earliest month gets to go first.

HTD6.speaker: Kronos
HTD6.text: These cards come in 12 suits, one for each month. But don't worry about the months, just match similar flowers. Same flower? Good. Different flower? Useless, don’t do that.

HTD7.speaker: Kronos
HTD7.text: On your turn, you pick one card from your hand and try to match it with a card on the field. Match = you capture both cards. No match? Then your card gets added to the field like sad leftovers.

HTD8.speaker: Kronos
HTD8.text: After you play a card, the game flips one card from the deck. If that card matches something on the field, you capture those too.

HTD9.speaker: Kronos
HTD9.text: Yes, two chances per turn. Easy, right? Even a stray cat like you can understand it.

HTD10.speaker: Kronos
HTD10.text: The goal is to make yaku--special combinations of cards. When you make a yaku, you score points. Points good. Losing bad. Simple. These are all the yaku you can make.

HTD11.speaker: Kronos
HTD11.text: And if your memory fails you, which it will, you can always check them from the Yaku list menu

HTD12.speaker: Kronos
HTD12.text: Now here comes the fun part, the dangerous part. When you complete a yaku, you get a choice: Koikoi or Shobu.

HTD13.speaker: Kronos
HTD13.text: If you choose Koikoi, you're saying: 'I want MORE points. I'm not done yet.' It's a gamble, your opponent can steal the round if they finish a yaku before you do.

HTD14.speaker: Kronos
HTD14.text: Risky… but delicious when it works.

HTD15.speaker: Kronos
HTD15.text: If you choose Shobu, you stop the round immediately. You take your points, safe and tidy, and the next round begins.

HTD16.speaker: Kronos
HTD16.text: No risk, no thrill, but hey, not everyone has the stomach for danger.

HTD17.speaker: Kronos
HTD17.text: The match lasts 3 rounds. At the end of all 3, whoever has the most points wins the entire game.

HTD18.speaker: Kronos
HTD18.text: So remember: Match cards, make yaku. Choose Koikoi if you're feeling lucky, choose Shobu if you're feeling scared.

HTD19.speaker: Kronos
HTD19.text: If your little cat brain needs a refresher, open the menu and choose Help and I'll repeat myself like a very handsome, very annoyed tutor.

HTD20.speaker: Kronos
HTD20.text: Time to play for real, good luck! You'll need it.
